summary: A stone tower first lit in June 1857 on a wave-swept island guarding Catalina Harbour and Trinity Bay; since 1956 wrapped in concrete, and still staffed.

access.note: Island station reached by boat or plane; grounds reported open, tower closed. Distant views from Seaview Drive, Catalina.

notes_for_editor: Mostly rests on one secondary source (Lighthouse Friends, which cites Journal of the House of Assembly of Newfoundland, not read directly) plus Parks Canada heritage texts. The Newfoundland Journals of the House of Assembly are not in the corpus (Marine Canada reports cover the Dominion, not pre-1949 Newfoundland). Register 4761 prints 1885 for full colonial status; the 1989 character statement says 1855. Character statement is dated 1991.12.16 while Lighthouse Friends says Recognized in 1990. Price listed 1967 but Ottawa Citizen 1984 says 18 years (about 1966). Sources differ on whether the light is lit and characteristic; List of Lights (Fl W 3.33s, year round) is current. Dyke 1981-2011 vs 'thirty years'. The 1893 inspector remark and Nugent 1844 quote are second-hand via Lighthouse Friends. Heritage lighthouse designation year (2015 in our record) not confirmed from a cached page. Fact-check: removed register 21133 building details (2003/1968/winch), not in cached page text.
